Rina Patel (People Ops): Hey folks — quick follow-up thread from today's all-hands about remote/hybrid, travel, offsites, and workspace policy. Drop questions here and I'll answer live / consolidate into the People Ops FAQ. :wave:
Ethan Monroe (Eng): Quick Q: For international offsites, do we reimburse per diem or actuals? Also flight class rules?
Rina Patel (People Ops): We reimburse actual receipts up to policy caps. Flights are standard economy for <=8h. Long-haul (>8h) can be upgraded to premium economy with manager + People Ops sign-off. Per diem is available for international multi-day offsites — we have a country list and rates in Concur.
Priya Sharma (Product): For quarterly hub days — if I'm in London, is there a travel stipend to get to the hub or is it on me?
Rina Patel (People Ops): Good Q — hub travel: we provide a hub-day travel stipend for non-local employees. Domestic hub stipend is $200, EMEA is $300, APAC varies by market (refer to doc). If it's an extended offsite (overnight), standard offsite budget applies instead.
Alex Chen (Infra): Any update on desk assignment in SF? A few infra folks would prefer dedicated desks because of daily on-call gear.
Rina Patel (People Ops): Dedicated desks are limited. Priority is given to on-call / hardware-heavy roles. Please fill the short form (workspace@redwood link in FAQ) and managers will be contacted for approval. Hot-desk remains default for most teams.
Maya Lopez (Sales): Team offsite budget question: what's the approval workflow and per-person cap if we rent a co-working space + meals?
Rina Patel (People Ops): Submit a pre-approval via the Offsite Request Form (link in the company handbook). Small team offsites (<=10 people): up to $500/person without exec approval — manager + People Ops approve. Larger events or >$500/person need Finance + People Ops sign-off. Include agenda and travel plan.
Cam Rivera (Security): For international travel on company business, does Redwood provide emergency medical/evacuation insurance?
Rina Patel (People Ops): Yes — we provide business travel insurance for approved company travel (medical emergency, evacuation). Personal vacation travel is not covered unless pre-approved as working travel. If you have specific destination concerns, loop in Security travel-alerts.
Ethan Monroe (Eng): If someone needs a visa letter for offsite travel, do we handle that?
Rina Patel (People Ops): Yes — People Ops can provide invitation/assignment letters for approved work travel. Start the request at least 6–8 weeks out for visa-heavy countries.
Priya Sharma (Product): Parenthood accommodations during offsites? Can we bring partners or request childcare stipends?
Rina Patel (People Ops): We encourage inclusive planning. Childcare stipends or reimbursements are considered case-by-case — include request in offsite pre-approval and we'll work with Finance. Bringing partners is generally allowed if budget covers it or individuals cover partner costs; disclose in the form.
Alex Chen (Infra): Any guidance on timezone-first remote-days vs hub-days for split teams?
Rina Patel (People Ops): Managers decide core hub-days for collaboration; global teams should aim for rotating hub-days to minimize unfair travel burden. We recommend at least one hub/week per quarter and use async work patterns otherwise. People Ops can help design equitable hub schedules.
Maya Lopez (Sales): Where will the FAQ live?
Rina Patel (People Ops): I'll add answers to the People Ops handbook (Confluence) and post a summarized thread in #people-ops. Also will pin the offsite request + expense links.

Rina Patel (People Ops): Great point, Cam — added requirement.
Ethan Monroe (Eng): :thumbsup: thanks Rina.

Rina Patel (People Ops): Thanks everyone — I'll update the handbook by EOD and follow up with any outstanding answers. If you want a private question, DM me or email workspace@redwood. :email:
